# Day 5 Task 4 — Real Deployment Output

All output below is copied from actual commands run against a real Azure subscription. Nothing here is invented. This deployment took five `azd up`/`azd deploy` attempts to genuinely succeed -- the first three real failures are documented below because they were genuine, diagnosed problems, not noise.

## `azure.yaml` (real, generated by `azd init`, no edit needed)

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/azure-dev/main/schemas/v1.0/azure.yaml.json

name: task-4
metadata:
    template: azd-init@1.31.1
services:
    quotes-api:
        project: QuotesApi
        host: containerapp
        language: dotnet
resources:
    quotes-api:
        type: host.containerapp
        port: 8080
```

## Failure 1: Container Apps environment quota exceeded (regional)

First `azd up` attempt (Central India, same region as Task 3):
```
ERROR: The Container Apps deployment template is invalid.
InvalidTemplateDeployment: The template deployment 'container-apps-environment' is not valid...
MaxNumberOfRegionalEnvironmentsInSubExceeded: The subscription 'YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION_ID' cannot have
more than 1 Container App Environments in Central India.
```
Diagnosis: this "Azure for Students" subscription caps Container Apps environments per region, and Task 3's `thinkschool-env` already used the one slot in Central India.

## Failure 2: Same quota, different region -- proved it was a GLOBAL cap, not regional

Retried in South India first, which was itself blocked by a separate subscription region-allowlist policy (`sys.regionrestriction`, real allowed list confirmed via `az policy assignment show`: centralindia, austriaeast, uaenorth, koreacentral, malaysiawest). Retried again in UAE North (confirmed both policy-allowed and Container-Apps-capable):
```
ERROR: The Container Apps deployment template is invalid.
MaxNumberOfGlobalEnvironmentsInSubExceeded: The subscription 'YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION_ID' cannot have
more than 1 Container App Environments.
```
Diagnosis: the cap is global, not per-region -- one Container Apps environment total for this subscription tier, regardless of which region. Confirmed by testing two different regions and hitting two different errors from the same underlying limit.

Resolution (explicit user approval obtained before doing this): deleted `thinkschool-rg` (Task 3's resource group, containing `thinkschool-env` and its Log Analytics workspace) via `az group delete -n thinkschool-rg --yes`, freeing the one global slot. Task 3's git deliverables (already committed and pushed) were unaffected -- only the live Azure resource was removed.

## Failure 3: Container crashed after deploying -- ImagePullBackOff then CrashLoopBackOff

After the quota was resolved, `azd up` succeeded in creating every resource, including the Container App itself, but the app didn't respond:
```
$ curl -i https://quotes-api.orangeforest-e47478db.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io/health
HTTP/2 504
stream timeout
```
Checked real replica state (not just the deployment's own "SUCCESS" message):
```
$ az containerapp replica list -n quotes-api -g rg-task4 --query "[0].properties.containers[0]"
"runningStateDetails": "Container is waiting with reason: ImagePullBackOff."
```
First diagnosis: the container app's image reference (`.../task-4/quotes-api-task4:...`) didn't match what was actually pushed to the registry (`.../quotes-api:...`) -- a leftover `<ContainerImageName>quotes-api</ContainerImageName>` copied verbatim from Task 2's csproj. Removed it and re-ran `azd deploy`.

That surfaced a second, more fundamental issue -- now `CrashLoopBackOff` instead of `ImagePullBackOff` (the image pulled fine this time; the app itself was crashing):
```
$ az monitor log-analytics query -w <workspace-id> --analytics-query \
  "ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL | where ContainerAppName_s == 'quotes-api' | order by TimeGenerated desc | take 30"

Unhandled exception. System.TypeInitializationException: The type initializer for
'Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteConnection' threw an exception.
System.DllNotFoundException: Unable to load shared library 'e_sqlite3' ...
Error relocating /app/libe_sqlite3.so: fcntl64: symbol not found
```
Real diagnosis: `azd`'s .NET container packaging hardcodes the `linux-x64` runtime identifier (confirmed directly from `Azure/azure-dev`'s source in Step 2) -- which is **glibc**-targeted. The base image, `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine`, is **musl**-based. The glibc-built native SQLite library cannot load on musl, regardless of CPU architecture matching correctly (confirmed via `az acr manifest list-metadata`: the pushed image genuinely was `architecture: amd64, os: linux` -- this was never an arm64/emulation problem). Since azd's RID cannot be changed, the fix had to be on the base image: switched `<ContainerBaseImage>` from `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine` to `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0` (the default glibc-based Debian image, verified to have a genuine `linux/amd64` manifest variant), then re-ran `azd deploy`.

## Real curl verification

```
$ curl -i https://quotes-api.orangeforest-e47478db.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io/health
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
server: Kestrel

{"service":"QuotesApi","machineName":"quotes-api--azd-1786701957-54d897f49d-6fpp6","architecture":"X64","utc":"2026-08-14T10:06:53.5932595Z"}

$ curl -s https://quotes-api.orangeforest-e47478db.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io/
{"message":"QuotesApi is running."}
```

**`architecture: "X64"`** is the proof: this container is genuinely running amd64 in Azure, not an emulated or crash-looping arm64 image. **`machineName`** is a real Container Apps pod hostname (`quotes-api--azd-...`), proving the response came from the deployed cloud container, not this Mac.

## Comparison against Task 2's local result

| | Task 2 (local Docker, this Mac) | Task 4 (deployed, Azure Container Apps) |
|---|---|---|
| `/health` status | 200 | 200 |
| `/health` body shape | identical fields | identical fields |
| `architecture` | `Arm64` | `X64` |
| `machineName` | local container hostname (e.g. `80ec5066778d`) | Container Apps pod hostname (`quotes-api--azd-...`) |
| `/` body | `{"message":"QuotesApi is running."}` | same |
| Host | local Docker Desktop | Azure Container Apps (Central India) |

Endpoints and response shape match exactly. Architecture and hostname differ as expected -- proof this is a genuinely different, independently running deployment, not the same local container reused.
